history.dynasty: Unknown; reconstructed in the Maratha/Peshwa era by Lord Bhate (knight of the Peshwa), per local travel sources
history.period: Antiquity unverified; Peshwa-era reconstruction; legend set in the deep past
history.summary: The Pundalik Temple honours Shree Pundalik, the legendary devotee credited with bringing Vithoba to Pandharpur and founding the Varkari sect - some scholars place the historical Pundalik in the early 12th century, persuading Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana to build the Pandharpur shrine, while others (Raeside, Vaudeville) dismiss him as mythical (historicity CONTESTED - verify). Legend says Pundalik, transformed by remorse for ill-treating his aged parents (witnessing the holy rivers as soiled women at Kukkutswami Ashram), devoted himself to serving them; when Krishna/Vishnu came to bless him, Pundalik asked the Lord to wait on a brick (vit) while he finished serving his parents - hence Vitthala standing arms-akimbo on a brick. The main five-storey temple (65 ft high, 63 ft broad, pyramidal gopuram, 25x17 ft portico) houses Vitthal flanked by Jaya and Vijaya, with a Shivling and Pundalik's idol in the portico; daily rituals are performed by Koli-community priests. A small samadhi shrine to Pundalik stands on the banks of the Chandrabhaga and is submerged when the river overflows. Customs include washing feet in a warm-water spring near the temple before darshan; an iron boat at the ghat is a local curiosity. Coordinates are APPROXIMATE (verify) - on the Chandrabhaga banks east of the Vitthal temple, 1.9 km east of Pandharpur Bus Stand.

name: Pundalik Temple
town_description: Pandharpur is a holy pilgrimage town in Solapur district of Maharashtra, on the banks of the Chandrabhaga (Bhima) River, often called the spiritual capital of Maharashtra and the Southern Kashi. It is the beating heart of the Warkari tradition: saints like Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram sang here, and millions of Warkaris walk here in processions (Dindis) for Ashadhi and Kartiki Ekadashi. The town is compact, temple-dense, and lives off pilgrim traffic.

travel.airport: Solapur Airport, ~75-78 km (verify; limited connectivity). Pune Airport, ~200 km (most practical).
travel.road: ~1.9 km east of Pandharpur Bus Stand, on the banks of the Chandrabhaga; auto-rickshaws from town.

visitor_information.best_time: June-July and October-November (yatra season); Mahashivratri is the big local celebration.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Darshan 4:00 AM - 7:00 PM per local travel source (verify). Wash feet in the warm-water spring near the temple before darshan, per custom.
